Control and integration platform

Blinky-Lite™

An MIT-licensed open-source platform for monitoring and controlling complex equipment, designed for remote access and reduced direct exposure of edge devices.

Watch the overview video Architecture and security Discuss your project

The platform

Connect equipment and expertise.

Blinky-Lite brings monitoring and control capabilities together so authorized people can see information and respond when their expertise is needed.

Developed by BL Monitor and Control AB and released under the MIT License.

Platform features

From device information to informed response.

Blinky-Lite brings device communication, monitoring, applications and access controls together in one platform.

Remote access

Use web applications to give authorized specialists access to equipment information and controls from desktops, tablets or mobile devices.

Alarms and notifications

Monitor equipment conditions and use alarm and notification capabilities to help teams respond when attention is needed.

Data and history

View device information and plots, and use data archiving and access and setting history to understand system activity.

Custom applications

Use the application builder and its library of cards and widgets to configure dashboards for your equipment.

Controlled access

Use authentication and role-based permissions to control access to applications and data. Security also depends on deployment and ongoing operation.

Device integration

Connect devices through publish-subscribe messaging and integrate their information into Blinky-Lite applications.

Built to adapt

Make the interface fit the equipment.

Different facilities need different views of their systems. Blinky-Lite includes an application builder for configuring dashboard applications and a framework for developing additional application components.

BL Monitor and Control can help integrate the platform with your equipment and develop solutions for your requirements.

Open source and integration expertise

Blinky-Lite is released under the MIT License. Customers can use and adapt the available code and choose how they obtain integration and support.

Open source does not guarantee future maintenance or support, but it gives customers options if their needs change.

Security architecture

Remote access, designed with security in mind.

Blinky-Lite uses publish-subscribe messaging. Devices initiate connections from inside the facility to a message broker, reducing the need for direct inbound access to edge devices.

Role-based permissions help restrict access to applications and data. Appropriate network protection, authentication, secure configuration and ongoing operation remain essential.

Explore the architecture and watch the video →

A layered approach

  • Devices initiate connections from inside the facility.
  • Components communicate using publish-subscribe messaging.
  • Role-based permissions help control access.
  • Deployment and operating practices remain important.
